Lab 7(A) - Laplacian Filter¶

In [1]:
import cv2
import numpy as np

from IPython.display import Image, display
from matplotlib import pyplot as plt

plt.rc('text', usetex=False)

Apply Laplacian Filter on Image to get Sharp Image¶

In [2]:
# ================ ( Laplacian Filter ) ===================


# 0. Image file path
imgFile = "moon.jpg"

# 1. Load image and convert to grayscale
img = cv2.imread(imgFile, 0)

# 2. Manually define the Laplacian Kernel
# This is the standard 3x3 kernel that detects horizontal and vertical edges
manual_kernel = np.array([
    [0,  1,  0],
    [1, -4,  1],
    [0,  1,  0]
], dtype=np.float32)

# 3. Apply the filter using filter2D
# Use cv2.CV_64F to avoid clipping negative values
laplacian_manual = cv2.filter2D(img, cv2.CV_64F, manual_kernel)

# 4. Take absolute value and convert back to 8-bit (0-255)
laplacian_abs = cv2.convertScaleAbs(laplacian_manual)

# 5. Sharpen: g(x,y) = f(x,y) - Laplacian  (center coefficient is NEGATIVE, so we subtract)
# Done in float and clipped, because uint8 "img + lap" wraps around above 255
finalImage = np.clip(img.astype(np.float64) - laplacian_manual, 0, 255).astype(np.uint8)

# 6. Display images
plt.figure(figsize=(12, 10))
plt.subplot(221), plt.imshow(img, cmap='gray'), plt.title('Original Image')
plt.subplot(222), plt.imshow(laplacian_manual, cmap='gray'), plt.title('Laplacian Image')
plt.subplot(223), plt.imshow(laplacian_abs, cmap='gray'), plt.title('Convert with Abs Scale')
plt.subplot(224), plt.imshow(finalImage, cmap='gray', vmin=0, vmax=255), plt.title('Final Image (Sharpened)')
plt.show()

Why the original img + laplacian_abs is wrong¶

img and laplacian_abs are both uint8, so NumPy addition wraps around (e.g. 250 + 10 = 4), creating black speckles on bright areas. Also, since the kernel's center is negative (-4), the correct sharpening formula is g = f − ∇²f. The comparison below shows the difference.

In [3]:
wrong = img + laplacian_abs                     # uint8 overflow (wrap-around)
saturated = cv2.add(img, laplacian_abs)         # saturates at 255 instead of wrapping

plt.figure(figsize=(15, 5))
plt.subplot(131), plt.imshow(wrong, cmap='gray'), plt.title('img + |lap|  (uint8 overflow)')
plt.subplot(132), plt.imshow(saturated, cmap='gray'), plt.title('cv2.add(img, |lap|)  (saturated)')
plt.subplot(133), plt.imshow(finalImage, cmap='gray', vmin=0, vmax=255), plt.title('f - lap  (correct sharpening)')
for ax in plt.gcf().axes: ax.axis('off')
plt.tight_layout()
plt.show()

print('Pixels that overflowed with img + |lap|:', int(np.sum(img.astype(int) + laplacian_abs > 255)))

Pixels that overflowed with img + |lap|: 541

Alternative kernel (includes diagonal edges)¶

In [4]:
# Alternative kernel: Detects diagonal edges as well
diag_kernel = np.array([
    [1,  1,  1],
    [1, -8,  1],
    [1,  1,  1]
], dtype=np.float32)

laplacian_diag = cv2.filter2D(img, cv2.CV_64F, diag_kernel)
finalDiag = np.clip(img.astype(np.float64) - laplacian_diag, 0, 255).astype(np.uint8)

plt.figure(figsize=(15, 5))
plt.subplot(131), plt.imshow(img, cmap='gray'), plt.title('Original')
plt.subplot(132), plt.imshow(finalImage, cmap='gray', vmin=0, vmax=255), plt.title('Sharpened (-4 kernel)')
plt.subplot(133), plt.imshow(finalDiag, cmap='gray', vmin=0, vmax=255), plt.title('Sharpened (-8 kernel, stronger)')
for ax in plt.gcf().axes: ax.axis('off')
plt.tight_layout()
plt.show()

Built-in cv2.Laplacian with Gaussian pre-blur¶

In [5]:
# ================== ( Laplacian Filter ) ===============

# 1. Optional: Apply Gaussian Blur to reduce noise
# This prevents the algorithm from picking up tiny details as edges
blurred = cv2.GaussianBlur(img, (3, 3), 0)

# 2. Apply the Laplacian Algorithm
# Use CV_64F to capture both positive and negative gradients (essential for edges)
laplacian = cv2.Laplacian(blurred, cv2.CV_64F)

# 3. Convert back to 8-bit image to view it properly
laplacian_8bit = cv2.convertScaleAbs(laplacian)

# 4. Subtract Laplacian from the original image (cv2.Laplacian uses the -4 center kernel)
finalImage2 = np.clip(img.astype(np.float64) - laplacian, 0, 255).astype(np.uint8)

# 5. Display images
plt.figure(figsize=(12, 10))
plt.subplot(221), plt.imshow(img, cmap='gray'), plt.title('Original Image')
plt.subplot(222), plt.imshow(laplacian, cmap='gray'), plt.title('Laplacian Image')
plt.subplot(223), plt.imshow(laplacian_8bit, cmap='gray'), plt.title('Convert with Abs Scale')
plt.subplot(224), plt.imshow(finalImage2, cmap='gray', vmin=0, vmax=255), plt.title('Final Image')
plt.show()

Laplacian on a simple shape (square + circle)¶

In [6]:
shape = cv2.imread('square.jpg', 0)

lap_shape = cv2.Laplacian(shape, cv2.CV_64F)
lap_shape_abs = cv2.convertScaleAbs(lap_shape)
sharp_shape = np.clip(shape.astype(np.float64) - lap_shape, 0, 255).astype(np.uint8)

plt.figure(figsize=(15, 5))
plt.subplot(131), plt.imshow(shape, cmap='gray', vmin=0, vmax=255), plt.title('Original')
plt.subplot(132), plt.imshow(lap_shape_abs, cmap='gray'), plt.title('|Laplacian| (edges only)')
plt.subplot(133), plt.imshow(sharp_shape, cmap='gray', vmin=0, vmax=255), plt.title('Sharpened')
for ax in plt.gcf().axes: ax.axis('off')
plt.tight_layout()
plt.show()

Observations¶

  1. The Laplacian is a second-derivative filter: it is zero in flat regions and responds strongly at edges and fine details (crater rims on the moon, borders of the square and circle). Flat areas of the square/circle image become black in the |Laplacian| image.
  2. The raw Laplacian contains negative values, so it must be computed in CV_64F; computing it in uint8 would clip all negative responses to 0 and lose half the edge information.
  3. Because the kernel's center is negative, sharpening is f − ∇²f. Adding instead of subtracting (and doing it in uint8) produces wrap-around artifacts.
  4. The −8 kernel (with diagonals) responds more strongly and gives a more aggressive sharpening than the −4 kernel, but also amplifies noise more.
  5. A small Gaussian blur before the Laplacian (LoG-like) suppresses noise so that only real edges are enhanced, giving a cleaner but slightly softer result.
